CHIEF COMPLAINT
Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a smoker with a 3-month history of intermittent cough that began after loading hay bales for his horses. He subsequently developed a cold which prompted him to visit his primary care physician. A chest X-ray was obtained to rule out pneumonia and revealed an incidental lung nodule. A CT scan was performed which confirmed the nodule. The patient was then referred to this clinic for further evaluation and management. His cough has since resolved. He denies current dyspnea or pain. The patient reports being quite anxious about this finding but remains engaged in care.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, dyspnea, or fever. Cough has resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Rheumatoid arthritis - fair control, no recent flares
2. Previous tobacco use - quit 7 years ago

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. Denies family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No family history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Quit smoking 7 years ago after many years of tobacco use. Currently denies tobacco use. Works with horses and loads hay regularly. Exercises regularly with frequent biking on trail systems. Reports good overall health and typically does not get sick.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, O2 saturation 98% on room air, afebrile
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally on auscultation
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no clicks, rubs, or murmurs, no extra beats appreciated
Extremities: Skin pink, warm, and dry. No edema to lower extremities. Mild swelling of knuckles on third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper lobe lung nodule, incidentally discovered. Plan for further workup and treatment: (1) Order pulmonary function tests to obtain baseline lung function assessment; (2) Schedule PET CT to determine metabolic activity of nodule; (3) Recommend video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for nodule removal with small portion of adjacent lung tissue. Procedure will involve three small incisions on right chest, performed under general anesthesia with estimated operative time of 1.5 hours. Postoperative admission for overnight observation with chest tube placement, to be removed at bedside the following day. Patient anticipated to be discharged on postoperative day 1. Continue rheumatoid arthritis management with rheumatologist and current medication therapy as previously outlined. Patient verbalized understanding and agreement with plan despite anxiety regarding procedure. Will obtain consent and proceed with paperwork.
